# NEWS / Economy

# Consumer Confidence Dips in August, Snapping a Three-Month Run

Jackson Moreland

Published Aug 14, 2026

###### Summary:

 Consumer sentiment fell to 51 in August from July's 55.2, ending a three-month stretch without a decline.
 Inflation expectations for the next year climbed to 4.3%, while the five-to-10-year outlook is 3.3%.
 July retail sales posted their steepest monthly decline in more than a year, and real average hourly earnings dropped 0.2% year over year. [...] The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment gauge fell to 51 in August, down from July's 55.2. That broke a three-month stretch without a decline, and it missed the 55 that economists had expected.
results.title: Consumer Confidence Dips in August, Ending Three-Month Gain

results.content: Higher gas prices may be among the economic headwinds taking their toll on Republican voters. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment survey found that Republicans’ consumer sentiment fell 9.5 points from July to August. This is one of the biggest monthly drops in the survey’s history, and it outpaced the overall decline in consumer sentiment of 8 percent.
